title: Upstream vs. downstream, and levels of prevention

blocks.text: A boy keeps falling into a river. You can keep rescuing him downstream, or you can walk upstream and find out who is pushing people in. Which saves more people?

chunks.text: **Downstream** actions respond after harm, such as ER care. **Upstream** actions change the causes, such as housing, clean air, and income. Upstream work usually takes longer to show results but prevents more illness.

**Primary prevention** stops a problem before it starts (vaccines). **Secondary prevention** catches it early (screenings). **Tertiary prevention** limits harm from an existing problem (managing diabetes).

steps.caption: Primary: nobody is sick yet. Stop the problem from starting.
Secondary: the illness is just starting. Catch it early.
Tertiary: the illness is established. Limit the harm.

blocks.title: Worked example: classify the program
steps: Situation: Free blood pressure checks at a community event.
Is anyone sick yet? Some people may have high blood pressure and not know it.
The program finds it early, so it is secondary prevention.
It is more upstream than ER care, but less upstream than raising incomes.

bullets: Upstream actions change causes. Downstream actions respond to harm.
Primary prevention stops problems before they start.
Tertiary prevention limits harm from existing problems.
